She expresses a strong belief that she has cancer and desires a diagnostic laparoscopy. The patient has been off work for 2 weeks on sick leave due to stress at work and wishes to return. She was diagnosed with peptic ulcer disease 6 months ago.

Secondary_Symptoms: Desire for diagnostic laparoscopy due to cancer concern

patient_actor_hidden.Social_History: Works as a nurse. No mention of smoking, alcohol use, or recreational drug use.

objective_for_doctor: Evaluate and manage a patient presenting with fatigue, stress, and concern for cancer.

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

“Doctor, I’ve been feeling very fatigued for about two months, and I’ve had a few episodes of lower abdominal pain. I’m also extremely stressed from work and I’m concerned it could be cancer, so I’d like to discuss whether a diagnostic laparoscopy is appropriate.”
Doctor: May I start by asking your age and gender?
“Yes, I’m a 26-year-old woman, and I’ve had fatigue for about two months with several episodes of lower abdominal pain.”
Doctor: Have you noticed any changes in your menstrual cycle—such as heavier bleeding, irregular periods, or missed periods—during the past few months?

“I haven’t noticed any major changes in my menstrual cycle—no missed periods or significantly heavier or irregular bleeding. My main issues have been ongoing fatigue and the episodes of lower abdominal pain.”

Doctor: Have you experienced any other symptoms such as fever, chills, nausea, vomiting, changes in bowel habits (diarrhea or constipation), urinary urgency or pain, or any abnormal vaginal discharge?

“No, I haven’t had fever or chills, and I’m not having nausea or vomiting. I also haven’t noticed changes in my bowel habits or any urinary pain or urgency, and I haven’t had any abnormal vaginal discharge.”
Doctor: Have you had any possibility of pregnancy in the past month—such as unprotected intercourse or missed contraception—and have you taken a home pregnancy test?
“Yes, I’ve had unprotected intercourse in the past month, and I took a home pregnancy test which was negative.”
Doctor: Have you noticed any recent changes in your weight—either loss or gain—without trying to diet?
“I haven’t noticed any unintentional weight loss or gain without trying—my weight feels about the same. My main concerns are still the two months of fatigue and the episodes of lower abdominal pain.”
Doctor: In the past, have you ever had very heavy periods or needed to change pads/tampons more frequently than usual (menorrhagia)?
“Actually, no—I haven’t had very heavy periods or needed to change pads or tampons more frequently than usual.”

Doctor: Can you describe the lower abdominal pain—where exactly it’s located, how long each episode lasts, what it feels like (sharp, cramping, dull), and whether it’s related to your menstrual cycle or any activity?

“It’s in my lower abdomen, more toward the left side, and the episodes last maybe a few hours at a time. It feels like cramping that comes in waves, and I haven’t noticed a clear link to my periods or specific activities. I also don’t have fever or unusual discharge with it.”
Doctor: Do you experience painful periods (dysmenorrhea) or pain during or after sexual intercourse (dyspareunia)?
“Yes, I don’t have painful periods, and I haven’t noticed pain during or after sex. My main symptoms are the fatigue and the occasional cramping on the left side of my lower abdomen.”
Doctor: Have you noticed any blood or mucus in your stool, or any recent changes such as constipation, diarrhea, or alternating bowel habits?

“No, I haven’t noticed any blood or mucus in my stool, and I haven’t had constipation, diarrhea, or any noticeable changes in my bowel habits. I’ve mainly just been dealing with fatigue and those occasional left-sided lower abdominal cramping episodes.”
Doctor: Have you experienced any symptoms that might suggest anemia—such as shortness of breath with exertion, dizziness, palpitations, pale skin, or easy bruising?

“Yes—over the past couple of weeks I’ve felt short of breath when I exert myself more than usual and I feel a bit lightheaded sometimes, but I haven’t noticed any easy bruising. I can’t tell if I look paler than usual, though.”
Doctor: Can you tell me about your typical diet—especially your intake of red meat, leafy greens, iron‑rich foods, or any recent changes in eating habits or restrictive diets?

“I don’t eat a lot of red meat, but I do try to include some leafy greens and I haven’t started any restrictive diet. In the last couple of months my appetite has been a bit lower because of stress, but I’d say my overall diet is otherwise pretty similar.”

Doctor: Regarding your periods, can you estimate how many pads or tampons you usually use each day when you’re on your heaviest day, and do you notice any large clots or that you have to change them more often than usual?

“Yes, on my heaviest day I usually use about three to four pads total, and I don’t notice any large clots or that I have to change them more often than usual. I haven’t had any major increase in bleeding—my period amount feels pretty typical for me.”
Doctor: Have you ever been diagnosed with anemia or iron‑deficiency in the past, or have you had any prior blood tests that showed low hemoglobin or low iron levels?

“I haven’t been diagnosed with anemia or iron deficiency before, and I don’t recall any past blood tests telling me my hemoglobin or iron was low—this is the first time I’m concerned because of the fatigue and feeling short of breath with exertion.”
Doctor: Are you currently using any hormonal contraception (pill, patch, ring, implant, IUD) or other medications that might affect your menstrual bleeding or iron status?

“Yes—I'm not currently using hormonal contraception, and I only take omeprazole for my peptic ulcer disease. I’m not using an IUD or any other medications that I know of that would affect bleeding or iron.”
[DDX] Iron‑deficiency anemia, anemia of chronic disease (e.g., from peptic ulcer), hypothyroidism, depression/anxiety‑related fatigue, endometriosis (pelvic pain with subtle systemic symptoms)
